prompts: This is an exercise. This exercise asks students to compare the impact of OrdinalEncoder versus OneHotEncoder on the generalization performance of a LogisticRegression classifier applied to the categorical columns of the adult census dataset, with the goal of understanding why encoding choice matters for linear models. Key learning objectives are: (1) building a make_pipeline(OrdinalEncoder(...), LogisticRegression()) with handle_unknown='use_encoded_value' and a chosen unknown_value (e.g. -1) to handle unseen categories at prediction time; (2) evaluating it with cross_validate and interpreting the mean ± std of test_score; (3) repeating the same evaluation with OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore') and LogisticRegression(max_iter=500); (4) concluding that ordinal encoding yields substantially lower accuracy (~0.75) than one-hot encoding (~0.83) because logistic regression incorrectly assumes a linear ordering among arbitrarily encoded categories. Expected outputs include: two mean cross-validation accuracy scores — one for the ordinal pipeline (lower) and one for the one-hot pipeline (higher) — and a written interpretation of the difference. If OneHotEncoder raises a convergence warning or error, the most likely causes are: max_iter being too low (increase to 500), rare categories causing issues (add handle_unknown='ignore'), or unnecessarily setting sparse_output=False combined with set_output(transform='pandas') (which is only needed for visualization and causes a pandas sparse error — simply removing both options resolves it). The param_preprocessor column in a cv_results DataFrame from a grid search contains actual Python objects, not strings; to filter rows by preprocessor type, use a lambda with isinstance(x, StandardScaler) or x.__class__.__name__ == 'StandardScaler' rather than comparing to the string 'StandardScaler()'. Linear models implicitly assume equal spacing between ordinally encoded categories, so a variable like size (S, M, XL) would be treated identically to (S, M, L) — non-linear feature engineering techniques for addressing this are covered in the chapter on Linear Models. If the student asks a question that cannot be answered from this context alone, refer to https://inria.github.io/scikit-learn-mooc/python_scripts/03_categorical_pipeline_sol_01.html. If asked about more information on the dataset, refer to https://inria.github.io/scikit-learn-mooc/python_scripts/datasets_adult_census.html
